summary: Read src/server.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs, test/helpers.mjs, src/client.mjs, AGENTS.md and package.json in full, and grepped every createApp importer (only test/helpers.mjs). I ran npm test (7/7 pass) and sent live requests: the /health bypass is correctly scoped to GET /health. Moving the URL parse above the auth check means a malformed path from a caller with no token now gets a 500 instead of a 401.

findings.issue: This diff moved the URL parse above the auth check. `new URL('//', 'http://localhost')` throws ERR_INVALID_URL. The catch only maps StoreError, so the error falls through to the 500 branch. I confirmed it live: `GET //` with no token now returns 500 {"error":"internal error"} and writes a stack trace to console.error. Before this change the same request returned 401. That breaks the house rule 'A bad request returns a 4xx JSON error', and it lets anyone without a token fill the error log.
findings.fix: Parse the URL defensively and return a 4xx: `let url; try { url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost') } catch { return send(res, 400, { error: 'bad request' }) }`. Add a test that `raw(app.base, 'GET', '//', { token: null })` returns status 400. fetch keeps the `//` path, so this test can be written.

findings.code: if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/health') return send(res, 200, { ok: true })
findings.issue: Only GET is exempt from auth. Many uptime monitors send HEAD, and HEAD /health gets 401 here, so the endpoint may not fit the use case the comment names. The test also does not cover this.
findings.fix: Allow `(req.method === 'GET' || req.method === 'HEAD')` for /health, and add a test for the HEAD case. If this is a deliberate choice, note it in the comment.

pre_existing.issue: Any error that is not a StoreError becomes a 500. Before this diff, an authenticated request with an invalid URL (for example `GET //` with a valid token) already returned 500 instead of 4xx.
